stem: How many surahs (chapters) are there in the Qur'an?

options.rationale: Correct: the Qur'an has 114 surahs.
Ninety-nine is the number of the beautiful names of God.
Thirty is the number of parts (juz) into which the Qur'an is divided.
Five is the number of Pillars and of daily prayers.

explanation: The Qur'an has **114 surahs**, each made of ayat (verses).

stem: Which is the first surah of the Qur'an?

options.content: Al-Fatihah
options.rationale: Correct: "the Opening".

options.content: Al-Ikhlas
options.rationale: Al-Ikhlas (Surah 112) is a short surah on the oneness of God.

options.content: Al-Baqarah
options.rationale: Al-Baqarah (Surah 2) is the longest surah and comes second.

options.content: Al-Qadr
options.rationale: Al-Qadr (Surah 97) is about the Night of Power.

explanation: **Al-Fatihah**, "the Opening", is the first surah and is recited in every cycle of the daily prayer.

options.content: A Muslim who has memorised the whole Qur'an
options.rationale: Correct: many Muslim children learn this in madrasahs.

options.content: A Muslim who has completed the Hajj pilgrimage
options.rationale: That person is a hajji.

options.content: A Muslim who leads prayer in the mosque
options.rationale: That is the imam.

options.content: A Muslim who gives the call to prayer
options.rationale: That is the muezzin.

explanation: A **hafiz** has memorised the whole Qur'an. A hajji has made the Hajj, an imam leads prayer and a muezzin calls to prayer.

options.content: The first chapter of the Qur'an, recited in every prayer
options.rationale: That is Al-Fatihah.

options.content: The standard copy of the Qur'an sent to the cities
options.rationale: That was made under Uthman.

options.content: The example of the Prophet, preserved in the Hadith
options.rationale: Correct: it is the way of the Prophet.

options.content: The pilgrimage made to Makkah each year
options.rationale: That is the Hajj.

explanation: The **Sunnah** is the example of the Prophet; the **Hadith** are the reports in which it is recorded.

stem: Which caliph first had the written parts of the Qur'an and the memories of the Companions gathered into one collection?

options.content: Uthman
options.rationale: Uthman had a standard copy made and sent to the main cities.

options.content: Abu Bakr
options.rationale: Correct: after the Prophet's death.

options.content: Umar
options.rationale: Umar is credited with suggesting the gathering, but the collection was made under Abu Bakr.

options.content: Ali
options.rationale: Ali was the fourth caliph.

explanation: **Abu Bakr** had the Qur'an gathered into one collection; **Uthman** later had a standard text copied and sent out.

stem: Nyasha sees her Muslim friend wrap the Qur'an in a cloth and place it on a high shelf. What does this practice show?

options.content: A belief that the book is a god to be worshipped
options.rationale: Muslims worship God alone, not the book.

options.content: Respect for what Muslims hold to be God's word
options.rationale: Correct: the book is treated with honour.

options.content: A rule that only scholars may read the Qur'an
options.rationale: Every Muslim is encouraged to read it.

options.content: A fear that the Qur'an will be damaged by sunlight
options.rationale: The reason is respect, not damage.

explanation: Muslims show **respect** for the Qur'an because they believe it is the word of God; it is not worshipped.
hints: Ask what the book is for Muslims.

stem: Why do Muslims use the Hadith as well as the Qur'an?

options.content: The Hadith replace the Qur'an when a command is difficult
options.rationale: The Hadith rank below the Qur'an.

options.content: The Hadith are the first revelation and the Qur'an came after
options.rationale: The Qur'an is the revelation.

options.content: The Hadith are used only by scholars and have no use in daily life
options.rationale: They guide daily practice.

options.content: The Hadith show how the Prophet applied it, such as how to pray
options.rationale: Correct: the Qur'an does not give every detail.

explanation: The Qur'an commands prayer, and the **Hadith** record how the Prophet prayed; they explain and apply the Qur'an but rank below it.
hints: Think of the details that the Qur'an itself does not set out.

stem: Which statement about the arrangement of the Qur'an is correct?

options.content: The surahs are arranged in the exact order in which they were revealed
options.rationale: The order is not chronological.

options.content: The shortest surahs come first and the longest come last
options.rationale: The arrangement is roughly the reverse.

options.content: The surahs are arranged by the names of the prophets they mention
options.rationale: They are not arranged this way.

options.content: The surahs run roughly from longest to shortest, not by date
options.rationale: Correct: Makkan and Madinan surahs are mixed.

explanation: The surahs are arranged roughly by length, longest first, apart from the opening surah; Makkan and Madinan surahs are mixed.
hints: Remember that Al-Fatihah is short but comes first by a special rule.

stem: Muslims believe that the Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet over about 23 years.
explanation: True. The revelation came in parts from about 610 CE until near the end of the Prophet's life.

stem: Muslims regard a translation of the Qur'an into English as the Qur'an itself.
explanation: False. Muslims hold that the Qur'an is the Arabic text; a translation is an attempt to give its meaning.

stem: Match each term with its meaning.

right.content: a report of what the Prophet said, did or approved
one who has memorised the Qur'an

explanation: Surah: chapter. Ayah: verse. Hadith: report of the Prophet. Hafiz: memoriser.

payload.template: The two most trusted Sunni Hadith collections are by {{blank:a}} and by {{blank:b}}.

explanation: **Sahih al-Bukhari** and **Sahih Muslim**, compiled in the ninth century CE.

stem: What name do Muslims give to the rules of reciting the Qur'an correctly?
explanation: **Tajwid** is the set of rules for correct recitation.

stem: Identify **three** ways in which Muslims show respect for the Qur'an.

points.description: They make wudu before touching the Arabic text
They keep it in a high, clean place or wrapped in cloth
They memorise and recite it correctly, or place it on a stand when reading

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Muslims make wudu before touching the Arabic text, keep it in a high, clean place wrapped in cloth, and memorise it or recite it correctly.

stem: Describe how the Qur'an was preserved after the Prophet's death.

points.description: It had been memorised by many Companions during the Prophet's life
It had been written on palm leaves, leather and flat stones
Abu Bakr had it gathered into one collection
Uthman had a standard copy made and sent to the main cities

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Many Companions had memorised the Qur'an and parts were written on palm leaves, leather and stones. Abu Bakr had it gathered into one collection, and Uthman had a standard copy made and sent to the main cities.

hints: Give the order: memory, writing, Abu Bakr, Uthman.

stem: Explain **two** reasons why the Hadith are important to Muslims.

points.description: They record the Sunnah, the example of the Prophet
Developed: Muslims believe the Prophet is the best model for living, so his actions guide daily behaviour
They explain details that the Qur'an does not give
Developed: the Qur'an commands prayer and fasting, and the Hadith show how the Prophet performed them

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The Hadith record the Sunnah, the example of the Prophet. Muslims believe he is the best model for living, so his actions guide their daily behaviour. They also explain details that the Qur'an does not give: the Qur'an commands prayer and fasting, and the Hadith show how the Prophet performed them.

explanation: Two reasons, each stated (1) and developed (2).
hints: Give a reason about example and a reason about detail.

stem:
**Source A** — a description (in words) of a lesson at a fictional madrasah in Gweru, 2026 (described in words; invented for this question)

> A group of children sit in rows on a carpet. Each child has a copy of the Qur'an on a small wooden stand. The teacher recites a verse in Arabic and the children repeat it. Afterwards the teacher explains the meaning in English and tells the children that the Prophet taught Muslims to be kind to their neighbours, and she says that this is found in the Hadith.

Study Source A and answer the questions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: According to Source A, where do the children place their copies of the Qur'an?

options.content: On the floor beside them
options.rationale: The source does not say this.

options.content: In a bag under the chair
options.rationale: The source does not say this.

options.content: On small wooden stands
options.rationale: Correct: the source says each copy is on a stand.

options.content: On the teacher's table
options.rationale: The source does not say this.

parts.explanation: The source says each child has a copy on a small wooden stand.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Using Source A, state **three** things the children learn in the lesson.

points.description: To recite verses of the Qur'an in Arabic by repeating after the teacher
The meaning of the verses in English
That the Hadith teach kindness to neighbours

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The children learn to recite verses of the Qur'an in Arabic by repeating after the teacher, learn their meaning in English, and learn from the Hadith that the Prophet taught kindness to neighbours.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why Muslim children learn to recite the Qur'an in Arabic.

points.description: Muslims believe the Qur'an in Arabic is the word of God, and a translation gives only the meaning
Prayer is performed in Arabic, so children need to recite the text
Recitation is an act of worship and keeps the text the same everywhere

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Muslims believe the Qur'an in Arabic is the word of God and that a translation gives only the meaning. Prayer is performed in Arabic, so children need to recite the text. Recitation is also an act of worship and keeps the text the same everywhere.

explanation: The source shows recitation, explanation and the Hadith used together.
hints: In (c) think of belief, prayer and unity.

stem: Tendai says: "The Qur'an is enough for a Muslim; the Hadith are not needed." Yusuf answers: "Without the Hadith we would not know how to pray."

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Outline **two** features of the structure of the Qur'an.

points.description: It has 114 surahs, each made of ayat
Surahs are arranged roughly from longest to shortest
Surahs are described as Makkan or Madinan according to when they were revealed
The first surah is Al-Fatihah

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The Qur'an has 114 surahs made of ayat, arranged roughly from longest to shortest, and the first is Al-Fatihah. Surahs are called Makkan or Madinan according to when they were revealed.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain why Al-Fatihah is important in Muslim worship.

points.description: It is recited in every cycle (rak'ah) of the daily prayer
It praises God and asks for guidance, so it sums up the relationship between a Muslim and God

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Al-Fatihah is recited in every cycle of the daily prayer. It praises God and asks for guidance, so it sums up the relationship between a Muslim and God.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Assess the view that the Qur'an is more important than the Hadith to Muslims.

points.description: For: the Qur'an is the word of God and the first source of authority; the Hadith rank below it
Against: the Hadith explain how to apply the Qur'an, for example how to pray and fast
Link: the two work together, and the Sunnah is the Prophet's living example of the Qur'an
A supported judgement

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant points or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge and examples, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.
Developed explanation of some factors or arguments with relevant supporting detail; a judgement is attempted but is only partly supported, or the other side is thin.
Some explanation of one or two relevant factors, or several points described with limited explanation; little or no judgement.
Simple, general or narrative statements with limited relevance to the question; little explanation.

answerSpec.modelAnswer: The Qur'an is more important in authority because Muslims believe it is the word of God, and the Hadith rank below it. However, the Hadith explain how to apply the Qur'an, for example how to pray and fast, so Muslims need both. The Sunnah is the Prophet's example of living by the Qur'an. I conclude that the Qur'an has greater authority, but the Hadith are needed for daily practice.

explanation: A strong answer separates authority from use and shows how the two work together.
hints: Separate authority from practical use before you judge.
